title: Single and coupled quantum van der Pol oscillators: Wigner-function dynamics, exact qutrit solutions, and synchronization
authors: Rohitashwa Chattopadhyay, Vinayak Pendse, Shamik Gupta
abstract: We study quantum van der Pol oscillator in which single-photon pumping competes with a nonlinear two-photon dissipative channel to produce a quantum limit cycle, and the question of how two such oscillators with non-identical intrinsic frequencies synchronize in the sense of phase locking when coupled dissipatively to one another. For a single oscillator, starting from a Lindblad description of the dynamics, we derive the exact Wigner-function evolution equation, and show that its Fokker--Planck approximation admits in the appropriate regime an equivalent classical Itô stochastic description that reproduces remarkably well the full Lindblad dynamics. Notably, the stochastic approach provides an efficient means of capturing system dynamics in the semiclassical regime, where a large number of energy eigenstates contribute and direct numerical simulations become computationally demanding. Restricting to the three lowest Fock states and using a parity symmetry, we obtain in closed form the stationary-state density matrix and its Wigner-function representation that displays pronounced nonclassical features. For two non-identical oscillators, we study the full Lindblad dynamics numerically and characterize synchronization through the stationary-state order parameter as a function of frequency mismatch and dissipative coupling. We find that increasing the effective nonlinear dissipative strength suppresses the synchronized region. Restricting the two oscillators to the three-level qutrit subspace, a parity symmetry reduces the stationary-state problem to an exact $41$-dimensional linear system, allowing to compute the synchronization order parameter. In this reduced description, results in the limit of large dissipation agree closely with those from the full dynamics, while exhibiting in the limit of small dissipation a double-peak synchronization structure accompanied by a phase reversal.
summary: This paper analyzes the quantum dynamics of van der Pol oscillators, first by deriving semiclassical approximations for the Wigner function, and then by studying the synchronization of two coupled units. It employs advanced techniques like symmetry reduction and solving linear systems to characterize synchronization, revealing rich non-trivial behavior in the quantum regime.
main_problem: The paper investigates the quantum dynamics and synchronization properties of coupled quantum van der Pol oscillators.
main_result: The analysis successfully derives semiclassical approximations for the Wigner function and characterizes synchronization using a reduced, parity-invariant linear system, revealing complex phase-reversal structures.
method: The study employs the Lindblad master equation, deriving Wigner-function evolution equations, utilizing Fokker-Planck/Itô stochastic approximations, and solving reduced linear eigenvalue problems based on symmetry constraints.
model_or_system: The model is the quantum van der Pol oscillator, described by a Lindblad master equation incorporating single-photon pumping and nonlinear two-photon dissipation. The analysis extends to two coupled, non-identical oscillators.
key_observables: Quantum limit cycle, stationary-state order parameter, Wigner function features (nonclassicality), and synchronization strength $|S|$.
important_parameters: Dissipation rates ($\gamma_1, \gamma_2$), frequency mismatch ($\Delta$), and coupling strength ($V$). Regimes include semiclassical limits and large/small dissipation limits.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on approximating the full quantum dynamics with stochastic/Fokker-Planck descriptions in the semiclassical limit, and reducing the Hilbert space to a qutrit subspace using parity symmetry for tractability.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the time evolution of the Wigner function and plot the synchronization strength $|S|$ and phase $\arg(S)$ in parameter planes for different dissipation regimes.
paper_structure: The paper first analyzes the single oscillator dynamics (Wigner function, Fokker-Planck, qutrit solution) and then extends the methodology to study the synchronization of two coupled oscillators, culminating in the solution of a reduced linear system.
why_interesting: This work bridges quantum optics (dissipative dynamics) with non-equilibrium statistical mechanics (synchronization), providing powerful tools (Wigner function, symmetry reduction) to analyze complex open quantum systems.
